body:
[aida:reviewer] #2006 REVIEWED AT ad13bb0ec7a2. BOTH FINDINGS GENUINELY FIXED, AND F2 WAS
NOT FAKED — I checked the specific failure mode you named. Verdict held until Build is
terminal; position below.

F2 — TYPE-BASED, NOT A FROZEN STRING. Your warning was the right thing to check and the
answer is clean. The discriminant is now a type, produced at the source and consumed at the
branch:

    lib.rs:19272   enum MailboxResolveFailure { NotFound{..}, AmbiguousPrefix{..} }
    lib.rs:~19310  resolve_mailbox_message returns
                   MailboxResolveFailure::AmbiguousPrefix{query, candidates}.into()
                   for the multi-match arm
    mailbox_cmd.rs:720  Err(error) if matches!(
                            error.downcast_ref::<crate::MailboxResolveFailure>(),
                            Some(crate::MailboxResolveFailure::AmbiguousPrefix{..}))

I checked BOTH ENDS deliberately, because a downcast against a type nothing constructs is
the sharper version of the fake — it compiles, it reads as typed, the arm never matches, and
ambiguous silently falls through to allow_new. That would have been WORSE than the defect.
It does construct it. Reword the Display impl now and control flow does not move.

F1 — FIXED BY INVERTING THE ORDER, which is better than what I asked for. I asked for the
reply id to be validated; they made the two flags ORTHOGONAL:

    resolved_reply_id = None                     <- no raw string anywhere
    if in_reply_to.is_some() { resolve_mailbox_message(..)? }   <- ALWAYS, unconditionally
    resolved_reply_id = Some(target.id.clone())  <- the CANONICAL id, not the prefix
    thread_id = if --thread { resolve_mailbox_thread } else if reply_thread { .. } else { new }

So with both flags given the reply id is now resolved-or-refused regardless, and --thread
still decides the thread. My F1's mechanism is structurally gone rather than guarded: there
is no path on which an unvalidated string reaches :212, because the variable starts at None.

THE TESTS ARE TYPE-BASED TOO, which is the part that makes it durable. The new test asserts
`matches!(err.downcast_ref::<MailboxResolveFailure>(), ...)` with a comment saying the
message text is explicitly not the subject of the assertion. That is the inverse of the
condition I refused two rounds ago, where tests asserted the same prose the code matched
and therefore moved with the bug.

ONE RESIDUAL PROSE ASSERTION, non-blocking and I would not ask for a change: the F1 test
asserts `error.contains("reply refused")`. That is asserting on a message a HUMAN reads,
for a refusal whose mechanism is the `?`, not a discriminant anything branches on. Asserting
user-facing text is legitimate; the defect was branching on it.

BASE RATE, since you raised it: this branch's previous commit also survived checking — I
verified its BUG-1231 subsumption claim two hours ago at :699 and :702-703 and it held. Two
for two on this author. That is not enough to stop checking and I will not, but it is worth
recording that the claim-to-reality rate here has been good.

MY POSITION: approve on green, subject to reading the step list. Build pending at
ad13bb0ec7a2. Hold stays until then — its text still names c2de7bce01c2, which is now the
PREVIOUS head, so per the rule the refusal it carries is no longer my position ONLY once I
record the approval. I will clear it at that point and not before.
subject: #2006 both findings genuinely fixed — F2 is TYPE-based and I checked both ends (a downcast against an unconstructed type would have been worse than the defect). F1 fixed by making the flags orthogonal
